fullPassage: The history of political philosophy in the West can be traced back to ancient Greece. The term polis, from which is derived the word political, refers to the city-state, the basic unit of government in ancient Greece. Early inquiries were concerned with questions such as “Which qualities make for the best leader?” “Which is the best system of government for a city-state?” and “What is the role of a citizen?” For many philosophers, the most fundamental moral questions—such as “How should I treat others?” and “What constitutes a good life?”—are the basis for corollary political considerations. The philosopher Aristotle (384–322 BCE) links the two through the concept of telos, which means “goal directed.” All things in life have a goal, or an end purpose, he says. It is the goal of human beings to live a good life, which is only achievable by living a life. Acquiring virtue is a difficult task, requiring constant practice. The acquisition of virtue necessarily involves a community to provide education, virtues, and provide opportunities for a person to behave virtuously. According to Aristotle, society is an essential part of living a good life, which involves a well-constructed political life: “This truth is attested by the experience of states: lawgivers make the citizens good by training them in habits of right action—this is the aim of all legislation, and if it fails to do this it is a failure; this is what distinguishes a good form of constitution from a bad one” (1996, 1103b20).

Early inquiries were concerned with questions such as “Which qualities make for the best leader?” “Which is the best system of government for a city-state?” and “What is the role of a citizen?” For many philosophers, the most fundamental moral questions—such as “How should I treat others?” and “What constitutes a good life?”—are the basis for corollary political considerations. The philosopher Aristotle (384–322 BCE) links the two through the concept of telos, which means “goal directed.” All things in life have a goal, or an end purpose, he says. It is the goal of human beings to live a good life, which is only achievable by living a life. Acquiring virtue is a difficult task, requiring constant practice. The acquisition of virtue necessarily involves a community to provide education, virtues, and provide opportunities for a person to behave virtuously. According to Aristotle, society is an essential part of living a good life, which involves a well-constructed political life: “This truth is attested by the experience of states: lawgivers make the citizens good by training them in habits of right action—this is the aim of all legislation, and if it fails to do this it is a failure; this is what distinguishes a good form of constitution from a bad one” (1996, 1103b20).
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: Aristotle links the two through the concept of telos, which means 'goal directed.' telos가 도덕과 정치를 잇는 '목표 지향적' 개념이라는 내용과 일치.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 거대한 제국 → polis는 the city-state(도시국가), the basic unit(기본 단위)
❌ ② 노력 필요 없음 → 덕은 constant practice가 필요한 difficult task
❌ ③ 고대 로마에서 시작 → 본문은 ancient Greece(고대 그리스)
✅ ④ telos = 목표 지향적, 도덕과 정치를 연결 — 본문과 일치 ←정답
det.tip: telos = 'goal directed', links moral & political

ch: polis는 고대 그리스에서 여러 도시국가를 통합한 거대한 제국을 가리킨다.
아리스토텔레스는 좋은 삶이 타고나는 것이어서 노력이 필요 없다고 보았다.
서양 정치철학의 역사는 고대 로마에서 처음 시작되었다.
telos는 '목표 지향적'이라는 뜻으로, 아리스토텔레스가 도덕과 정치를 잇는 개념이다.
